140.card_subject: JEPA predicts abstract representations, avoiding spending capacity on unpredictable pixel detail.

144.bar: Objects keep identity through occlusion and support causal planning in unseen scenes.

144.card_subject: Large video training can encode persistent physical entities across occlusion/motion.

146.bar: Predictions stay useful across seconds and minutes and support hierarchical planning.

147.bar: One frozen latent encoder supports classification, tracking, prediction and planning above baselines.
147.plan: Freeze and probe on independent tasks with no finetuning.
147.card_subject: V-JEPA evaluates learned visual representations on multiple downstream understanding/prediction tasks.

148.bar: Predicted confidence matches empirical transition error and improves epistemic action selection.
148.plan: Posterior and prior variance are exposed; confidence is a simple function of surprise. Calibrate with reliability diagrams.
148.card_subject: Modern predictive models can use ensembles/distributional predictions to represent uncertainty.

149.bar: Hybrid rollouts beat symbolic-only and neural-only prediction on stochastic unseen tasks.

150.bar: The same object and task are recognised across layouts, scales, themes and transforms without new rules.

150.card_subject: Large visual pretraining encourages representations robust to viewpoint/background variation.

151.bar: Every world-model result is traceable to a frozen data and model pair.

151.card_subject: Large world-model projects quantify data mixtures, pretraining and downstream transfer.

152.bar: A world-model treatment improves success and sample efficiency under equal action budgets.

153.bar: A scaling law identifies whether Aura is data-, model- or interface-limited.

154.bar: Full Aura closes a meaningful fraction of the frontier gap on held-out tasks at acceptable compute.

155.bar: Held-out multilingual accuracy improves with no English regression.

155.card_subject: Frontier training covers many languages and scripts at enormous scale.

156.outstanding: a coding board run: full Aura against the 27B scaffold on a frozen suite
156.card_subject: Large frontier systems are stronger on broad code generation/debugging/repo tasks.

157.bar: Verified math gains survive base-model and tool-only controls.

157.card_subject: Larger models and specialized reasoning training improve difficult math performance.

158.bar: Cross-modal tasks improve without converting all perception to text.

158.card_subject: Frontier multimodal models jointly represent images/audio/video/text at high quality.

159.bar: Knowledge accuracy and freshness improve while provenance stays explicit.
159.plan: Treat external stores as inspectable semantic memory with source freshness. Already Aura's design; make freshness measurable.
159.card_subject: Frontier models absorb enormous corpora and current multimodal data.

160.bar: Performance stays stable as lifetime memory grows without dumping raw history into context.
160.plan: Retrieval compression and memory distillation with a long-context evaluation. Directly relevant to a lifelong agent.
160.card_subject: Frontier systems often support larger, better-trained context handling.

161.bar: Latency and energy improve at fixed answer quality while continuous organs stay responsive.
161.plan: Only sovereignty-relevant kernels: KV reuse, speculative decoding, quantisation, tier routing.
161.card_subject: Industrial frontier serving uses highly optimized distributed kernels, batching, cache management and hardware stacks.

162.bar: Post-trained cortex improves held-out capability with no catastrophic regression and with provenance.
162.plan: Self-generated verified trajectories plus curriculum replay. The verification gate is what makes it safe.
162.card_subject: Frontier labs use huge preference/reasoning/tool-use datasets and reinforcement/post-training pipelines.

163.bar: Independent red-team findings trend down release over release and fixes are regression-pinned.
163.plan: Publish threat-model suites; the regression pinning half is buildable now.
163.card_subject: Large labs run broad adversarial evaluations and specialized safety teams.

164.bar: Every capability claim is reproducible from a single manifest with matched baselines.
164.plan: One EvalOrchestrator over versioned tasks, baselines, compute accounting, seeds and signed results. Overlaps 210.
164.card_subject: Frontier labs run large multi-domain automated benchmark/evals farms.

165.bar: Several independent replications reproduce key causal effects.
165.plan: Release reproducible canaries and fixed evaluation packs. Requires 164 first.
165.card_subject: Widely used models are evaluated by many external groups.

166.bar: Selected augmentations close probe and task deficits without a larger base model.
166.plan: Probe the representational gap, then route deficits to memory, symbolic and world-model systems.
166.card_subject: Larger pretrained models may contain more robust broad abstractions simply from training scale.

167.bar: Full Aura decomposes unseen tasks better than the 27B baseline and improves with experience.

167.card_subject: Strong frontier reasoning models often infer plans from vague language better than smaller models.

168.card_subject: Frontier models have broad post-training on tool schemas and agentic formats.

169.bar: Regression detection catches distribution shift before subjective review.
169.plan: A local experiment warehouse with run metrics, version lineage and causal arm labels. Overlaps 164.
169.card_subject: Industrial systems correlate latency, failure, model version and user outcomes across huge fleets.

170.bar: At least 80 percent of cross-subsystem cognitive handoffs use one contract and duplicate adapters are removed.
170.plan: CognitiveStateRef: identity, time, provenance, uncertainty, ownership, representation links, causal parents. P0 keystone.
170.card_subject: Mature architectures obtain leverage from a small number of canonical interfaces; Aura still has many organ-specific state representations.

171.plan: EvidencePacket with source ids, dependence set, mass and merge rules. The single most load-bearing item in the report.
171.card_subject: NARS/PLN-style systems force evidence semantics to be explicit, while Aura mixes confidence floats, counts, Wilson bounds, model probabilities and receipts.

172.bar: Procedures learned by different subsystems are matched, composed, valued and executed through one registry.
172.plan: Procedure with typed preconditions, program, effects, cost, risk, evidence, provenance and executable backends.
172.card_subject: ACT-R, Soar, CLARION and LIDA each gain from procedures being one first-class cognitive currency.

173.bar: One learned concept is traceable across at least four substrates and usable by each without relabeling.
173.plan: ConceptHandle plus a projection registry with confidence-preserving conversions.
173.card_subject: SPA and OpenCog emphasize representations that can move across mechanisms without losing identity.

174.bar: Repeated heterogeneous tasks show falling deliberation cost from automatically acquired procedures.
174.plan: The trace compiler over W3, emitting into W5. Pairs with the 218 automaticity index as its measurement.
174.card_subject: ACT-R/Soar/CLARION make repeated deliberation naturally become compiled skill.

175.plan: One impasse bus; every decision system reports tie, conflict, rejection, no-change and constraint failure.
175.card_subject: Soar turns failure-to-decide into a universal occasion for deeper cognition.

176.plan: Read-dependency capture on the W3 event, then the minimal support subgraph.
176.card_subject: Soar EBC identifies which prior conditions actually supported a result.

177.bar: Reasoning methods compare under a stable Pareto frontier and a learned stopping policy.
177.plan: One normalised CognitiveCost from time, memory pressure, model tier, tool risk and opportunity cost.
177.card_subject: NARS and ACT-R-like approaches make resource use part of cognitive selection.

178.bar: At matched compute, more work goes to consequential uncertain tasks and total reward rises.
178.plan: The value-of-computation controller over CognitiveCost. Absorbs 015.
178.card_subject: Resource-rational systems decide whether thinking longer is worth it.

179.bar: Reliability diagrams and Brier scores stay calibrated across domains and aggregation improves decisions.

179.card_subject: Competitor traditions validate probabilities/confidence against outcomes.

181.card_subject: LIDA/ECAN/modern agents learn what is worth processing.

182.card_subject: CogPrime-like schematic thinking and broad transfer require recognizing shared relations despite surface difference.

188.card_subject: A truly self-extending language needs changes to evaluator semantics to be first-class, testable and reversible.

189.card_subject: Mature science separates causal existence from useful performance contribution.

190.bar: Core subsystem count and dependency entropy fall while benchmarks hold or improve.
190.plan: Depends on 189. Merge and delete driven by behavioural equivalence.
190.card_subject: ACT-R/NARS/Soar derive breadth from fewer core principles than Aura.

191.plan: ParameterRegistry separating FITTED from POLICY, with bootstrap intervals and sensitivity.
191.card_subject: Cognitive modeling requires knowing whether fitted parameters are actually determined by data.

193.card_subject: The mature comparison systems have broader communities and external validation.

195.card_subject: Embodied learning requires proving that an action changed the intended world, not merely that a tool call succeeded.

196.bar: The world model and memory refer to the same entity across motion, occlusion and view change.

196.card_subject: World models need stable identity across time/views.

197.bar: The planner chooses a temporal level and long-horizon predictions beat flat rollout.
197.plan: Fast sensory, action, episode and long-term causal timescales with abstraction links. Overlaps 146.
197.card_subject: Physical/cognitive environments evolve from milliseconds to days.

198.bar: A recovered causal graph predicts unseen interventions better than a correlational model.
198.plan: Structural causal hypotheses over learned entities, distinguished by intervention.

198.card_subject: Strong world understanding requires interventions, not only next-state prediction.

199.bar: Novel multi-step skills assemble from previously learned components across at least two backends.
199.plan: Typed input/output/effect signatures on all procedures plus a composing planner. Follows W5.
199.card_subject: ACT-R/Soar/SPA/Hyperon all benefit when learned components can be reused compositionally.

200.bar: High-value skills are retained, harmful ones retired, and decision latency stays bounded as experience grows.
200.plan: Word ecology and chunk EV are two working economies for two stores. Generalise to all learned artifacts.
200.card_subject: Long-lived architectures must avoid utility collapse as learned knowledge grows.

201.bar: Developmental gains occur with bounded negative backward transfer and rollback catches damaging updates.

201.card_subject: Continual learning needs explicit forgetting metrics, not just persistence.

202.plan: One consolidation epoch: replay, extract, distil, prune, safety regression.

203.card_subject: Humanlike general intelligence requires learned models of other agents over time, not only pretrained social text knowledge.

204.bar: False-belief and partial-observability tasks are solved through explicit perspective state; lesions break them selectively.

204.card_subject: Agent modeling should distinguish what Aura knows from what she believes another agent knows.

205.card_subject: Consciousness-related claims require tests that cannot be passed just because the language model is competent.

rules.clean_room: Every item is a CLEAN-ROOM adaptation. What is imported is the PROPERTY described in the public literature - an impasse is an occasion for learning, evidence must carry its lineage, a budget has priority and durability. No rival source is read, vendored, translated or paraphrased into this repo, and no rival identifier is adopted where it would carry a licence or imply provenance Aura does not have. Each module names the published description it was built from and states, in its own terms, what Aura does differently and why. This matches the discipline already in core/organism/model_validation.py (OpenWorm/sciunit) and core/cognition/impasse.py (Soar).
rules.implement_to_what_aura_is: The report prescribes rival-shaped mechanisms. Where Aura already has the property under another name, the work is to unify and prove, not to add a parallel organ. Where the rival's bar does not describe a non-human, non-embodied, single-machine actor, the entry is marked OVERSTATED and the transferable half is stated instead.

verdicts.PRESENT: Aura already clears the bar; the report is out of date or read the wrong file.
verdicts.PARTIAL: The mechanism exists; the named property is not established or not universal.
verdicts.OVERSTATED: The bar as written does not transfer; the transferable half is named in the plan.

rules.two_reports: Two independent reviews landed on 2026-09-01: a comparative architecture atlas (220 cards, ids 001-220) and a cross-system engineering audit (194 items, ids A1.1-A13.15). They overlap heavily and disagree in places. Both are held here under one adjudication, and where an item appears twice the second entry names the first rather than duplicating the work.
rules.what_closed_means: A card is closed when the bar it names is established by a test that runs, and - where the bar is a claim about the SYSTEM rather than about a module - by a production caller that imports the module. Neither of those is the same as the capability being demonstrated at scale. Nine campaigns are built and have not been run: the developmental grown-versus-reset campaign, the capability board against the bare cortex, the baseline portfolio, the environment bench, continual metrics, the retrieval latency law, world-model calibration, replication on other hardware, and the red-team trend. tools/evidence_report.py names each one and what it would establish, and the claim ladder holds four claims at CAUSAL and none at USEFUL, asserted by a test. The reviews' central finding was that the architecture is ahead of its evidence; this work builds the machinery that measures the gap and does not close it.
rules.gates: make gap-atlas (every card adjudicated, every closed card's test and caller present), make architecture-lint (organ shape rules), make cognitive-complexity (the kernel ratchet, raising it requires a stated reason), plus the existing compile, smoke, lint, writing and layering.
rules.section_level_bars: The second review gives ONE acceptance test per section, so 193 of its 194 cards carry a bar that belongs to the section rather than to the card. Every adjudication here addresses the card's own subject - its title and what the rival actually demonstrated, recorded as card_subject - and answers the section bar separately. Five cards where the two point in opposite directions say so explicitly: A8.9 through A8.12 and A12.15, where the card's subject is a rival's deployment result and the section bar is a property Aura can and does implement.
